text:
incident-bot: ALERT triggered: high kv-cache evictions on prod-cluster-7 (shard group a1). severity: P1. Paging surge + continuous-batching spike.

olivia (oncall): saw the alert, joining. paging rate jumped ~4x at 13:07 UTC, latency tail climbing.

samir (eng-runtime): on it. early hypothesis: quantized kernel path selecting int8 AWQ kernels with larger KV footprint for recent gptq variants -> cache pressure.

anya (eng-ml): confirmed: model variant rollout from staging->prod 12:45 had AWQ quantization artifact that increases kv size by ~2.3x on long contexts. metrics: kv_mem_per_shard up from 1.2GB -> 2.8GB.

matt (sre): customer-facing impact? ryan, any spikes in error pages?

ryan (support): we have three customers reporting higher 5xxs and latency SLO breaches. Not systemic 100% but high-value customers A and C affected. Escalating to account reps.

olivia (oncall): quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle continuous-batching for affected pools 2) force kernel selection to fp16 fallback for AWQ/gptq models 3) roll back the model variant if needed. Which is fastest?

samir (eng-runtime): fastest is throttling batching and forcing kernel fallback. Rollback is heavier (re-deploy). I'll push a hotfix route config to reduce batch size and disable cont-batching for pool a1.

eng-ml-bot: NOTE: model: redwood/gptq-13b-awq-v2 deployed -> observed kv_bytes_per_token change.

samir (eng-runtime): pushing temporary hotfix: set `continuous_batching.max_batch_size=8` and `kv.eviction_threshold=0.72` for pools [a1,a2]. Applying now.

Code snippet (hotfix applied):
```bash
# runtime config API
curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/v1/pools/a1/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' \
  -d '{"continuous_batching":{"max_batch_size":8,"min_latency_ms":5},"kv":{"eviction_threshold":0.72}}'
```

matt (sre): command accepted, nodes reloaded. Observability: eviction rate down at 13:14 UTC, latency tail dropping in 2m.

olivia (oncall): second mitigation: kernel forcing. samir, can you toggle kernel selection to prefer fp16 for the AWQ/gptq families?

samir (eng-runtime): yes. adding rule: `kernel_policy.model_name_prefix="gptq" -> kernel_family=fp16_fallback`. Deploying.

anya (eng-ml): note: fp16 will increase per-token compute slightly but reduces kv footprint because we avoid int8 packing bug. OK to proceed.

samir (eng-runtime): kernel rule applied at 13:19 UTC. sample logs: 
```
[13:19:02] routing: model redwood/gptq-13b-awq-v2 -> kernel fp16_fallback (was awq_int8_fast)
[13:19:03] runtime: kv_size_estimate reduced by ~48% on new sessions
```

ryan (support): customers A and C reporting improvement. A dropped error rate from 2.6% -> 0.4% in 10m.

olivia (oncall): good. still need full postmortem: root cause, regression window, rollout gating. Also confirm if this affects all quant paths (int8/awq/gptq) or only AWQ variant. Anya?

anya (eng-ml): preliminary: AWQ kernel codepath introduced an aggressive packing optimization that mis-calculated kv index offsets for long contexts, causing kv blobs to be padded and stored per-token at larger sizes. It interacts badly with our continuous batching because more requests have warm KV and get larger allocations. I suspect gptq-int8 also touches similar packing but less severe.

samir (eng-runtime): adding follow-ups: - revert the packing change in awq kernel in canary - add unit tests for kv footprint regression - improve kernel selection heuristics when estimated kv_size/sec > threshold - expose kv_size_per_model metric to console

matt (sre): operational follow-ups: - add autoscale guard to warm pool to prevent paging cascade - alert rule: kv_eviction_rate > 200/min -> auto-throttle batching - add chaos test for quant kernel rollouts

olivia (oncall): customer comms: prepare a brief for account team summarizing root cause and ETA for rollback. Ryan, can you draft?

ryan (support): drafting now. Key points: incident started 13:07 UTC, mitigated by 13:25 UTC, partial rollback decision pending. Customers told to expect follow-up within 2 hours.

eng-ml-bot: metric snapshot: 
- peak_kv_evictions: 486/min
- avg_cont_batch_size_pre: 42 -> post-hotfix: 9
- kv_mem_shard_avg_pre: 2.78GB -> post: 1.4GB

samir (eng-runtime): deploying permanent mitigations next: 1) roll back the AWQ packing patch in canary, 2) add kernel fallback auto-policy if kv_mem_estimate > 1.6GB, 3) maintain reduced batch defaults for 24h.

olivia (oncall): handoff: I will stay on for 30m to confirm stability, then hand to matt for overnight monitoring. samir/anya, please update the incident tracker with root cause and action items.

matt (sre): acknowledged. will keep an eye on paging alerts and customer escalations.

olivia (oncall): final quick note: add short-term dashboard card for 'kv_bytes_per_active_session' and roll out alert `kv_bytes_per_session > 1.8GB` -> page eng-runtime.

samir (eng-runtime): added alert. leaving follow-up tasks in Jira: JIRA-ENG-3912 (awq-pack-revert), JIRA-OPS-2177 (batch-throttle-autoscale), JIRA-ML-1083 (kv-footprint-tests).

ryan (support): will send customer update at 14:00 UTC with mitigation summary.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. severity downgraded to P2 at 13:27 UTC.

---
Notes for postmortem: include exact commit that introduced packing change, deployment timeline, heatmap of affected customers, memory deltas per model variant, and proposed rollout gating for quant kernels.
